title: Climate model shows large-scale wind and solar farms in the Sahara increase rain and vegetation

settings.description: Coarse-resolution climate model with dynamic vegetation applied to the Sahara, the most arid parts of the Arabian Desert, and the neighbouring Sahel.
Control experiment with no wind or solar installations, giving a Sahara precipitation baseline of 0.24 mm/day.
Large-scale wind farm installation covering the Sahara, generating about 3 TW.
Large-scale solar farm installation covering the Sahara with 15 per cent panel conversion efficiency, generating about 79 TW.
Wind and solar farms deployed together in the Sahara.
Additional wind farm experiments that separate the climate change induced by the initial roughness change from that induced by the subsequent vegetation-albedo feedback.
Solar farm sensitivity experiment at 45 per cent conversion efficiency, at which effective albedo rises above the background desert albedo.
Solar farm sensitivity experiment at an intermediate 30 per cent conversion efficiency.
Experiment expanding wind and solar farms from the Sahara to the world's other deserts.
Wind farm experiments using checkerboard and quarter spatial configurations within the Sahara.
The Sahel transition region reported separately from the Sahara because it is highly sensitive to land change.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: The wind farm causes significant regional warming of near-surface air temperature of +2.16 K.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Wind-farm warming is larger in minimum than in maximum temperature (+2.36 versus +1.85 K) because turbines enhance vertical mixing and bring warmer air down during stable nights.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. Only the mean +2.16 K response was captured, so the timing dependence is lost.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Wind farms increase precipitation by up to +0.25 mm/day over installation areas, doubling the 0.24 mm/day control value.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Sahel precipitation increases by +1.12 mm/day under the wind farm experiment.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Vegetation cover fraction increases by +0.084 under the wind farm experiment.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Leaf area index increases by +0.50 m2/m2 under the wind farm experiment.

claims.from: large-scale wind farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Root carbon increases by +0.08 kgC/m2 under the wind farm experiment.

claims.from: increased surface drag from wind turbines
claims.statement: Increased surface drag from the turbines reduces wind speed by about 36 per cent.

claims.from: recovered vegetation in the wetter Sahel
claims.statement: A slight cooling is observed in the wetter Sahel because recovered vegetation increases evaporation and decreases sensible heat flux, opposing the regional warming.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is a within-experiment sign reversal, the exact case the counting rules require to be kept separate.

claims.from: increased surface friction reducing wind velocity and Coriolis force
claims.to: surface and moisture convergence toward the Saharan heat low
claims.statement: Increased surface friction reduces wind velocity and the associated Coriolis force, leaving a dominant pressure gradient toward the Saharan heat low that produces surface convergence, upward motion, moisture convergence and higher humidity.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is the paper's stated dynamical mechanism for the wind-farm rainfall increase.

claims.from: large-scale solar farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Solar farms increase surface air temperature through direct albedo reduction and the resulting albedo-precipitation-vegetation feedback.

claims.from: large-scale solar farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Solar-farm warming is stronger in maximum temperature (+1.28 K) than in minimum temperature (+0.97 K) because albedo reduction mainly affects net radiation during daytime, the opposite asymmetry to wind farms.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the contrast with the wind-farm nighttime asymmetry is unavailable to the graph.

claims.from: large-scale solar farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Solar farms raise precipitation at farm locations in the Sahara by +0.13 mm/day, a 50 per cent increase over the control.

claims.from: large-scale solar farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Sahel precipitation increases by +0.57 mm/day under the solar farm experiment.

claims.from: large-scale solar farm in the Sahara
claims.statement: Unlike the wind farm experiment, the solar farm experiment produces very little change in wind speed.

claims.from: combined wind and solar farms in the Sahara
claims.statement: Combined deployment raises Sahara precipitation from 0.24 to 0.59 mm/day, about a 150 per cent increase.

claims.from: combined wind and solar farms in the Sahara
claims.statement: Combined deployment raises temperature by +2.65 K, only slightly more than the solar farm alone.

claims.from: combined wind and solar farms in the Sahara
claims.statement: The most substantial precipitation increase occurs in the Sahel, between +200 and +500 mm/year.

claims.from: surface roughness increase from turbines
claims.statement: Roughness change contributes +1.00 K of the wind-farm warming, because wind reduction weakens near-surface vertical turbulent transport.

claims.from: vegetation feedback through albedo reduction and roughness increase
claims.statement: Vegetation feedback contributes +1.16 K of the wind-farm warming, almost equal to the roughness contribution.

claims.from: vegetation feedback
claims.statement: Vegetation feedback supplies 80 per cent of the wind-farm precipitation increase (+0.20 mm/day), with roughness acting mainly as the initial trigger.

claims.from: surface albedo decrease from solar panels
claims.statement: Lower panel albedo increases absorbed solar radiation and surface warming, lowering surface pressure and producing convergence, rising motion and more precipitation.

claims.from: solar panel conversion efficiency of 45 per cent raising effective albedo
claims.statement: If panel efficiency is high enough to raise effective albedo above the background, the climate impact reverses to surface cooling with precipitation suppression.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. The sign of the solar-farm effect depends on this condition, so its absence makes the extracted solar claims unconditioned.

claims.from: solar panel conversion efficiency of 30 per cent
claims.statement: An intermediate 30 per cent conversion efficiency produces negligible albedo change and therefore insignificant climate impacts.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A null result that the counting rules require to be kept.

claims.from: expanding farms from the Sahara to the world's other deserts
claims.statement: Expanding wind and solar farms from the Sahara to the world's other deserts does not significantly increase the climate impact.

claims.from: other deserts with scattered distribution, smaller size and weaker albedo change
claims.statement: The impact is not significant in many other deserts because of their scattered geographical distribution, smaller sizes and weaker albedo changes, so the effect is particular to the Sahara.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is the paper's own statement that its headline result is location specific.

claims.from: spatial configuration of the farms, checkerboard versus quarter
claims.to: spatial distribution of the climate impact
claims.statement: Even within the Sahara the impacts depend on the specific location and spatial distribution of the farms, with uneven impacts under checkerboard and quarter configurations.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, although spatial configuration is exactly the property scenario design needs.

claims.from: omission of vegetation feedback from the model
claims.statement: The authors conclude that models without vegetation feedback would considerably underestimate the temperature and precipitation impacts of large-scale Saharan wind farms.
